newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: African bank agrees loans of $44 million for roads.
newsitem.headline: African bank agrees loans of $44 million for roads.

text.p: The African Development Bank (ADB) said it had extended loans totalling more than $44 million for road projects in Benin, Mauritania and Eritrea.
A bank statement said the loans marked a resumption of such lending after an interruption of 2-1/2 years pending the reconstitution of the ADB's soft-loan fund concluded in May.
The loan terms were not stated.
The Benin loan of $23.3 million will finance the rehabilitation of the 27-km (18 miles) Cotonou-Porto-Novo road.

Mauritania's $13 million credit is for the construction of a tarmac road from Akjout to Atar. It is part of a $26 million trans-Maghreb road project to boost trade between the Arab Maghreb and Sub-Saharan Africa.
The $7.9 million loan for Eritrea will go towards the rehabilitation of the Asmara-Tesseinei road.
The Benin and Mauritania projects are subject to international tender.
